# lean-pkg claims rebase

move claims.yaml and coverage.yaml to a new manuscript version: carry unchanged statements re-keyed from the new .aux, list the rest for review; writes only --out-dir; never changes a status.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims rebase --from-tex OLD.tex --to-tex NEW.tex --to-aux NEW.aux
                       [--from-aux OLD.aux] [--from-sha256 HEX]
                       [--to-version arXiv:IDvN] [--to-commit HEX] [--to-repo URL]
                       [--unwrap-macro NAME] [--claims-file PATH] [--coverage-file PATH]
                       [--out-dir DIR] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--from-tex OLD.tex` | the (flattened) TeX the claims were written against; its SHA-256 must match coverage.yaml's manuscript sha256 (an arXiv version: a .tex of its source-baseline record), or --from-sha256 when none is recorded. Required. |
| `--to-tex NEW.tex` | the new version's (flattened) TeX. Required. |
| `--to-aux NEW.aux` | the .aux of a full build of NEW.tex: new numbers and pages come from it. Required. |
| `--from-aux OLD.aux` | the old .aux: resolves references written as numbers (Lemma 4.2, (3.7)) to TeX labels |
| `--from-sha256 HEX` | the SHA-256 of OLD.tex, required when coverage.yaml records none (checked, never trusted) |
| `--to-version arXiv:IDvN` | the new manuscript.version for the proposed coverage.yaml |
| `--to-commit HEX` | or: the manuscript repo commit of NEW.tex (sha256 is NEW.tex's) |
| `--to-repo URL` | with --to-commit: the manuscript repo (default: coverage.yaml's) |
| `--unwrap-macro NAME` | also read \\NAME{X} as X (a revision-highlight macro); repeatable |
| `--claims-file PATH` | a working-copy claims file instead of the one committed at HEAD |
| `--coverage-file PATH` | a working-copy coverage file instead of coverage.yaml committed at HEAD |
| `--out-dir DIR` | write the proposals, the report and the review packet here (a new or empty directory); without it nothing is written |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims rebase NAME --from-tex OLD.tex --to-tex NEW.tex --to-aux NEW.aux` | move `claims.yaml` and `coverage.yaml` (committed at `HEAD`) to a new manuscript version (#6); never writes the registry or the checkout, never changes a claim status, never sets `fixed_in`. Refused (exit 1): `OLD.tex`'s SHA-256 differs from the manuscript `sha256` `coverage.yaml` records, or is none of the `.tex` hashes of the source-baseline record of its arXiv version (`formalization anchor`; none recorded: `--from-sha256` must state it; the proposal drops `manuscript.eprint_sha256`), TeX that is not UTF-8 or has unbalanced environments, a referenced label defined twice in `OLD.tex`, `NEW.tex` or `NEW.aux`. Each referenced label (coverage `paper.label`, else `paper.number` via `--from-aux`; a finding's `location.label`; a label in a `citation`) is classified by its statement or equation environment, compared after a fixed normalization: `unchanged` (carried; number, page and line re-keyed from `NEW.aux`), `changed`, `missing`, `moved-into-proof`, `not-in-old`, `unsupported`, `unnumbered`; all but `unchanged` need review and stay as they were. `--out-dir DIR` (new or empty) gets the proposed `claims.yaml` and `coverage.yaml`, `rebase-report.json` (`claims-rebase/1`) and `.md` with old/new excerpts, `review/` excerpts and diffs, and `MANIFEST.sha256`; deterministic; without it nothing is written. Exit 0 all carried, 1 review needed or refused, 2 usage; `--json` {ok, counts, labels[], rows[], findings[], citations[], needs_review[], proposed_errors[], files[], ...}. [Move to a new manuscript version](../prior-art.md#move-to-a-new-manuscript-version) | `[--from-aux OLD.aux]` `[--from-sha256 HEX]` `[--to-version arXiv:IDvN \| --to-commit HEX [--to-repo URL]]` `[--unwrap-macro NAME ...]` `[--claims-file PATH]` `[--coverage-file PATH]` `[--out-dir DIR]` `[--json]` |

## JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `claims-rebase` (exit 0): `citations`, `counts`, `files`, `findings`, `inputs`, `labels`, `name`, `needs_review`, `normalizations`, `ok`, `out_dir`, `proposed_errors`, `rows`, `statuses_changed`, `to_version`, `warnings`, `written`

## Examples

Compare each label the claims and coverage.yaml committed at HEAD refer to between the old and the new TeX, and write the proposed claims.yaml and coverage.yaml, the report and the review excerpts into the new or empty rebase-v2; it never edits the checkout or the registry and exits 1 when anything needs review.

```bash
lean-pkg claims rebase my-proof --from-tex old/paper.tex --to-tex new/paper.tex --to-aux new/paper.aux --from-aux old/paper.aux --to-version arXiv:2510.01234v2 --out-dir rebase-v2
```

The report only (no --out-dir, nothing written), stating the old TeX's SHA-256 because coverage.yaml records none; a mismatch is refused.

```bash
lean-pkg claims rebase my-proof --from-tex old/paper.tex --to-tex new/paper.tex --to-aux new/paper.aux --from-sha256 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef --json
```
